Tutorial: the one-dimensional test

Source: vignettes/articles/Tutorials_onedim.Rmd
Tutorials_onedim.Rmd
library(selectiveHotelling)

selective_truncated_F() computes a second selective pp-value, ppolar,1dp_{\mathrm{polar,1d}}. It holds fixed everything about the tested observations except one angle, the one that determines Hotelling’s T2T^2. Its reference distribution is then a truncated FF distribution in one dimension, which makes it faster to compute. The price is power: fixing more of the data leaves less room to detect a difference (the technical details).

set.seed(123)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2), matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) + 3,
           matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) - 3)
init <- c(1, 51, 101)
cl_fun <- function(x) kmeans_with_fixed_init(x, init_centers_idx = init)$cluster
cl <- cl_fun(X)

Any clustering algorithm

With clustering = "custom", the test takes the same clustering function as selective_hotelling_bc() and computes the pp-value by a Monte Carlo path in one dimension:

res1d <- selective_truncated_F(X, 1, 2, clustering = "custom", method = "bc",
                               cl_fun = cl_fun, cl_obs = cl, M = 1000)
c(onedim = res1d$pval, classical_F = res1d$p_uncond)
#>      onedim classical_F 
#>  0.02469193  0.00000000

p_uncond is the classical FFpp-value, which ignores the clustering.

A closed form for kk-means

For kk-means, the pp-value can be computed exactly, without Monte Carlo, if we also condition on the whole sequence of assignments made by Lloyd’s algorithm:

res_exact <- selective_truncated_F(X, 1, 2, clustering = "kmeans", method = "exact",
                                   K = 3, init_centers_idx = init)
res_exact$pval
#> [1] 0.04102747

This version conditions on the most, and it is the least powerful of the three tests.

Which test to use

Test Function Conditions on Speed Power
ppolarp_{\mathrm{polar}} selective_hotelling_test(), selective_hotelling_bc() the clustering slowest highest
ppolar,1dp_{\mathrm{polar,1d}} selective_truncated_F(method = "bc") the clustering and all but one angle faster lower
ppolar,1dtrajp_{\mathrm{polar,1d}}^{\mathrm{traj}} selective_truncated_F(method = "exact") also the kk-means trajectory instant lowest

All three control the selective Type I error. We recommend ppolarp_{\mathrm{polar}} unless computing time is a constraint.
